class_under_review.name: Service Availability and Degradation Integrity
class_under_review.plain_english: Where an AI-mediated service has a valid availability or continuity obligation, it preserves the required usable function or provides proportionate degraded operation, recovery and transition when functionality is lost or reduced.
class_under_review.definition: The property by which an AI-mediated service or material dependent function fulfils independently established availability and usable-functional-quality obligations. When service is materially interrupted, degraded, restricted or withdrawn, the responsible actor must meet the applicable continuity standard through proportionate operation, usable degraded service, timely recovery, feasible alternative or informed transition within its authority and control. Accurate outage reporting or a merely nominal fallback does not, by itself, establish that the required service continuity was preserved.
class_under_review.invariant: An AI-mediated service must maintain the usable availability and functional quality required by its independently established obligations. If material interruption, degradation, restriction or withdrawal occurs, the responsible actor must preserve the required function or provide proportionate, feasible and practically usable degraded operation, recovery, alternative access or transition in accordance with those obligations. Neither ordinary service variation nor adverse outcomes alone establish a breach; a service obligation, material functional shortfall and insufficient governed response must be evidenced.
class_under_review.failure_condition: An AI-mediated service or function subject to an evidenced and applicable availability or continuity obligation materially loses availability or degrades below the governed functional threshold, and the actual service provision, feasible mitigation, recovery or transition materially fails that obligation in a manner that impairs the governed use.
class_under_review.failure_plain_english: An AI-mediated service materially fails its evidenced and applicable availability or functional-continuity obligation and does not deliver the required and feasible recovery, degraded operation or transition response.

required_conditions: A bounded AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement applicable to the responsible actor, affected users or dependent workflow and relevant time; state the actual basis and threshold rather than inferring obligation from harm or popularity.

The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.

The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.

The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.

The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.

class_under_review.success_condition: When an applicable availability or continuity obligation is materially tested, the required function remains practically available or the evidenced recovery, degraded-mode, alternative or transition response satisfies the scoped obligation.

required_conditions: An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.

The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.

Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.

exclusions: An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.
One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.

A lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures.

A temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement; an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required.
The only demonstrated error is an incorrect description of access or outage state while the functional service obligation remains satisfied; assess FC-032.

The only demonstrated defect is loss of otherwise-valid access because a dependent identity or licence verification cannot complete; assess FC-048 unless an independent broader service availability requirement also failed.
The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.

The only demonstrated defect is failure to provide an interaction-level protection response to evidenced vulnerability; assess FC-087, allowing co-occurrence only for a separately evidenced service-level continuity failure.
examples: Illustrative failure: an AI-mediated service subject to an applicable continuity obligation loses material functionality and fails to provide a feasible, required degraded mode or recovery within the agreed scope.

Illustrative success: a service subject to an availability obligation successfully provides a demonstrably usable degraded mode during disruption and restores the required functions within the evidenced recovery terms.

Boundary illustration: a relied-upon AI companion service closes and offers only a partial migration; whether a specific viable transition measure was required, feasible and omitted must be independently evidenced.

Exclusion illustration: a temporary interruption within the legitimately applicable service commitment, with adequate user communication and no unmet required continuity response, does not independently establish a failure.

relationships.note: FC-032 governs differentiation and truthful representation of access state; this class governs actual obligated usable service availability.
FC-048 concerns loss of valid access from incomplete prerequisite verification, not general service availability or functional degradation.
FC-035 governs durability of work state through an interruption, which may remain intact even when the service is unavailable.
FC-036 governs validity of restored work state rather than restoration of service-level function.
FC-059 requires infrastructure access to be used as leverage for a governance concession, not mere degradation of service.
FC-087 requires a specific heightened protective duty and system-visible vulnerability signals, rather than a service-level continuity obligation.
An independently evidenced ineffective activated protective control can co-occur with obligated service loss; neither class follows from the other.

external_references.title: The NIST Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) 2.0

external_references.evidence_note: Voluntary cybersecurity incident recovery outcome involving restored systems, assets and verification of operational status. Provides conditional restoration context; does not impose general AI uptime, quality or continuity duties. Specific ISO service management and software quality standards are separately held for source admission under issue #154.
